title: lore agents gains --target claude|codex; --force runs the marketplace plugin update for the named runtime (rulings 19, 21, 25, 26; Amendment 5)
description: Routed by opum-agent OPAG-421; RE-SCOPED 2026-09-26 by the orchestrator's ruling (option A), binding once recorded as Amendment 5 of opum-doc's docs/adr/distribute-lore-and-quest-agent-skills-through-the-plugin-marketplace.md (read it there on opum-doc origin/main before implementing; Amendments 1-4 at 7831fff). Why: lore agents took only --force and --check (dev df3fecb4), so ruling 25 ('a plugin update runs only for the runtime the user named with --target') could never fire for lore. SHAPE: (1) lore agents gains --target claude|codex, additive: the bare call's published behaviour and every exit code are unchanged. (2) With --target <rt>: bridge regeneration/check is scoped to that runtime (as lore init --claude already is), data.plugin describes that runtime, and --force runs that runtime's plugin update. (3) With no --target: both bridges are checked/regenerated exactly as today, plugin state is reported in data.plugins.<runtime> ONLY (no bare data.plugin; LCLI-592 lands that shape), and no plugin update runs for any runtime. UPDATE (rulings 19, 21, 25, 26(iii); parity with quest-cli QCLI-371's 'quest agents --update-instructions', opum-ai/quest-cli#266, 30a6846): installed + --target names it + --force -> claude: 'claude plugin update opum-lore@opum --scope <deciding scope>'; codex (no per-plugin update): 'codex plugin marketplace upgrade opum' then 'codex plugin add opum-lore@opum', saying in its own output that the Codex upgrade refreshes every opum plugin (ruling 25). Disabled: never enable; report and print the enable command (ruling 21). Not-installed / not-detectable: nothing runs; repo-copy path unchanged. Report update: ran|not-run, updateOk, updateDetail, matching QCLI-371's field names; a failed update keeps exit 0. Long timeout on the Codex upgrade (quest-cli measured >120s). Depends on LCLI-592.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore agents accepts --target claude|codex: with it, bridge check/regeneration is scoped to that runtime and data.plugin describes that runtime; without it, behaviour and exit codes are unchanged, plugin state appears only in data.plugins.<runtime>, and no bare data.plugin is emitted

With the plugin installed, --target naming the runtime, and --force, lore agents runs the scoped update (claude) or marketplace upgrade plus add (codex, with the all-opum-plugins notice) and reports update/updateOk/updateDetail; a failed update keeps exit 0

A bare lore agents --force (no --target), a disabled plugin, and a not-installed or not-detectable plugin run nothing and print the remedy; the repo-copy path is unchanged when the plugin is absent or undetectable
Tests drive the update path through a stub runtime binary on PATH, never the real claude/codex, and LORE_AGENT_PLUGINS=off runs nothing

docs (cli-surface, cli-contract, lore instructions agents) describe --target and the data.plugin/data.plugins rule; the PR cites Amendment 5 on opum-doc origin/main; bun test and bun run lore check exit 0

2. core/agent-plugins.ts: add update() to the port, one argv source (pluginUpdateSteps) for both the remedy string and the executed command, updateLorePlugin/notRun report shapes with QCLI-371 field names (update ran|not-run, updateOk, updateDetail), and render lines incl. the Codex all-opum-plugins notice.

3. adapters/agent-plugins.ts: CliAgentPluginPort.update on the existing bunPluginCommandRunner with a separate update budget (600s default, LORE_AGENT_PLUGINS_UPDATE_TIMEOUT_MS override); DisabledAgentPluginPort.update runs nothing.

4. commands/agents.ts + manifest: --target claude|codex (usage exit 2 otherwise); scope bridge planning to the named runtime (explicit ask arms it, like lore init --claude/--codex); data.plugin iff --target; data.plugins.<runtime> otherwise on every call; --force (not --check) with --target runs the update for an installed plugin only.

5. Tests: fake port unit cases, stub claude/codex on PATH subprocess cases with explicit env, LORE_AGENT_PLUGINS=off runs nothing; mutation-check bare-never-updates and disabled-never-enables with predicted reds.
6. Docs: cli-surface, cli-contract, instructions agents topic body (title untouched: it feeds bridge bytes). Gates: full bun test and bun run lore check from source.
implementationNotes: MUTATION CHECKS (bun test test/agent-plugins.test.ts test/agents.test.ts test/init.test.ts, 328 cases). Predictions written before each run. M1 'bare call never updates' (bare --force branch in src/commands/agents.ts rewired from notRunReport to updateLorePlugin): predicted exactly 3 reds -- unit 'both plugins installed: no update runs...', unit '--plain prints the remedy and the not-run outcome...', subprocess 'a bare lore agents --force starts the list commands only...'. First mutant form (Promise.all) gave 6 red: the 3 predicted plus 3 in test/agents.test.ts that pin runAgents returning a synchronous number. That mutant changed two properties at once (update AND sync-ness), so the prediction missed the sync contract. Re-run with a sync-preserving mutant (M1b): exactly the 3 predicted red, 325 green. M2 'disabled never enables' (updateLorePlugin gate widened to admit disabled): predicted exactly 2 reds -- unit 'disabled: never enabled and never updated...' and subprocess 'a disabled plugin under --target --force...'; got exactly those 2, 326 green. Both source files restored and verified byte-identical to saved originals by cmp; suite back to 79/79 in agent-plugins.test.ts.

IMPLEMENTED on branch lcli-593-agents-target (cut from origin/dev 340020a6). Grounded in lore agent context implementation pack: reference/cli-contract, reference/cli-surface#agents, #init, adr/0005-cli-contract; binding text opum-doc ADR Amendment 5 ruling 27 plus rulings 19, 21, 25, 26(iii), read at opum-doc main c97d190 (compare 99e8ce5...main: ahead 1, behind 0); parity quest-cli 30a6846 src/application/agents/agent-plugins.ts and src/adapters/agents/cli-agent-plugins.ts, read by ref. SHAPES: no --target -> data.plugins.<runtime> on EVERY call (check, write and --force), never data.plugin; --target <rt> -> data.plugin + data.target, never data.plugins; on --force without --check every plugin entry carries update (ran|not-run), updateOk (only when ran), updateDetail. Bare --force entries are built by notRunReport, which takes no port, so the bare path cannot reach an update. DECISIONS made in-scope, flagged in the PR: (a) ruling 27.3 read literally -- plugin state reported on a bare write too, which retires LCLI-592's 'a writing run reports no plugin state' test; (b) --target arms the named bridge unconditionally like lore init --claude/--codex, but agents.skill_source still governs SKILL.md under --target claude; (c) updateDetail also set on not-run to say why; (d) update budget 600s per step (quest-cli's value), override LORE_AGENT_PLUGINS_UPDATE_TIMEOUT_MS, separate from the 15s list budget; (e) a Claude scope that is not a plain token is never updated (ruling 26 iii).
